meta.note: Rule rows (PWC25 shape): id, world, statement (paraphrased), locators, speaker, mechanism, seam (AB code), derives (blocked slugs a playable model exists for), default_dial_reason, licence. Proposals: a batched reader (gpt-6-luna) read the books in shards of about 8,000 words; nothing here was human-checked, and no source text is kept.

rules.statement: A core character begins with 8 points in each of Might, Speed, and Intellect, plus 6 points to distribute among those pools. Spending pool points activates abilities or improves actions; Edge reduces the pool cost, and a core character’s Edge is 0 in each stat.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Your Three Stats; Edge (cypher-rd#000)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to pools as the spendable reserve and Edge as a discount; a world can change starting reserves or discounts to make abilities more or less costly.

rules.statement: A core character can record up to three wounds of each severity. Minor wounds have no penalty; when that track is full, another minor wound becomes moderate. Taking the last moderate wound hinders all actions, and later moderate wounds become major; each major wound hinders all actions, and taking the last one causes death.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Wounds (cypher-rd#000)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to escalating injury tracks with action penalties and death at the final major wound; a world can adjust the track lengths or consequences to change how lethal injury is.

rules.statement: A trained skill eases related tasks, while specialization eases them by two steps; training in the same skill twice grants specialization. An inability hinders related tasks, and an expert can ease a task by three steps, usually through a special ability.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Skills (cypher-rd#000)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to training and specialization as cumulative task advantages, with inabilities as disadvantages; a world can vary which skills can be learned at each tier.

rules.statement: Applying Effort costs 3 points from the relevant Pool and eases a task by one step per Effort applied. A core character has Effort 1, so can ease a task by only one step this way.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Effort (cypher-rd#000)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a three-point cost for one step of task improvement; a world can raise the cost or Effort limit to make exceptional performance rarer.

rules.statement: An asset usually eases a task by one step; a particularly good asset or two ordinary assets can ease it by two steps. Assets cannot ease a task by more than two steps in total.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Asset (cypher-rd#000)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a maximum two-step benefit from assets; a world can change that cap to reflect how much equipment, assistance, or favorable circumstances can help.

rules.statement: A character can hold at most two cyphers at once. Each cypher is a one-use ability; after using one, the character receives replacements when the GM decides.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Cyphers (cypher-rd#000)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to two single-use abilities carried at a time and discretionary replacement; a world can change the capacity or replacement rate to control access to temporary effects.

rules.statement: A core character’s recovery restores a number of Pool points equal to a roll of 1d6 plus tier, distributed among Pools as desired but not beyond their normal maximum. Pool points can be recovered through rest and recovery; wounds can be healed through rallying, treatment, or rest.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Recoveries; Healing Wounds (cypher-rd#000)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a tier-scaled recovery roll and several ways to heal wounds; a world can change recovery timing or methods to make resource loss more or less persistent.

rules.statement: A core character uses light weapons without an attack penalty, but attacks with medium or heavy weapons are hindered. Wearing any armor hinders some physical tasks for a core character, while shields are usable by any character.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Weapons and Armor (cypher-rd#000)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to weapon and armor familiarity imposing task penalties; a world can vary which characters avoid those penalties to represent training or equipment handling.

rules.statement: An ability that keeps affecting its user ends when the user chooses, as a free extra action on their turn; effects specified to last until recovery instead end when recovery begins.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Genre Character Abilities from Types and Foci — Action or Enabler (cypher-rd#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to ending a continuing effect freely on the user’s turn; a world can make effects harder to dismiss, at the cost of player control.

rules.statement: Each level of Effort used on an ability buys one listed improvement; separate listed improvements require separate levels, and the user can usually apply Effort to ease a roll or add attack damage even when the ability has no extra-cost marker.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Genre Character Abilities from Types and Foci — Effort (cypher-rd#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one improvement per Effort level; a world can change the cost of scaling effects, reflecting how demanding power use is.

rules.statement: In optional real-world action play, characters can take two additional minor wounds and one additional moderate wound. Treatment takes a Last action for a minor wound, one minute for a moderate wound, and ten minutes for a major wound.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Optional Rules for Real-World Action Games (cypher-rd#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the added wound capacity and listed treatment times; a world can remove the bonus or lengthen treatment to make action less heroic.

rules.statement: While a character has at least two moderate wounds or one major wound, Desperate Actions grant one free reroll on one action each round, as though spending 1 XP.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Optional Rules for Real-World Action Games — Desperate Actions (cypher-rd#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one free reroll per round when badly hurt; a world can change the wound threshold or remove the benefit, trading heroic resilience for danger.

rules.statement: A starting real-world character has no type or focus, and so receives none of their extra Pool points, Edge, or abilities; they also cannot use medium or heavy weapons without hindrance unless starting skill training cancels that inability for a specific weapon class.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Creating a Real-World Character (cypher-rd#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to no type or focus and an inability with medium and heavy weapons; a world can permit such training at the start, reflecting a character’s background.

rules.statement: Real-world wound treatment takes ten minutes for a minor wound, one hour for a moderate wound, and one week for a major wound.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Creating a Real-World Character — Wound Treatment (cypher-rd#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the longer, realistic treatment times; a world can shorten them to support faster-paced heroic play.

rules.statement: In a dungeon-fantasy game, wound treatment takes one minute for a minor wound, ten minutes for a moderate wound, and one hour for a major wound.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Creating Dungeon Fantasy Characters — Wound Treatment (cypher-rd#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the listed fantasy recovery times; a world can lengthen them to make injuries more consequential.

rules.statement: A Barbarian who has at least three moderate wounds or one major wound gains one free Effort level for one attack each round, rising to two free levels at tier 3.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Barbarian Abilities — Wounded Fury (cypher-rd#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to granting free attack Effort only at the stated injury threshold; a world can adjust the threshold or bonus, changing how injury fuels combat.

rules.statement: Healing Hand reduces one wound by one severity step: minor wounds disappear, moderate wounds become minor, and major wounds become moderate. The recipient cannot exceed the limit for the lower-severity wound; each use costs 1 Intellect more than the previous use until a recovery resets the cost to 1.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Cleric Abilities — Healing Hand (cypher-rd#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one-step wound reduction with rising Intellect cost; a world can change how much healing is possible, because divine power is tiring or scarce.

rules.statement: A beast companion is a level 2 follower no larger than its druid, and follows instructions. If it dies, the druid can spend resources to revive it or search for and befriend another; the companion’s movement depends on its creature type.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Druid Abilities — Beast Companion (cypher-rd#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one level 2 companion; a world can alter its size or level, because the companion’s bond and availability set the limit.

rules.statement: A necromancer can animate a nearby dead creature about their size or smaller as a level 1 follower, with no memories, intelligence, or former special abilities. It obeys verbal commands until the necromancer takes a recovery of at least one hour, then becomes inert; animating another body makes the first inert, and damage carries over if it is reanimated.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Necromancer Abilities — Basic Necromancy (cypher-rd#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one active corpse follower lasting until an hour-long recovery; a world can change capacity or duration, because animation requires ongoing necromantic control.

rules.statement: Preparing a low-power manifest cypher takes ten minutes and grants its effect as a spell that costs 2 Intellect to cast; unlike a cypher, the spell remains after use and does not count against the cypher limit. A ten-hour recovery can replace the prepared spell and ends durations from the old one; at tiers 3 and 6, medium and advanced cyphers become available for 4 and 6 Intellect respectively.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Mage Abilities — Prepare Spell (cypher-rd#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one prepared low-power cypher spell; a world can raise the available power or number prepared, because learning and holding arcane effects takes time and mental reserves.

rules.statement: Friend to Small Creatures influences a named type of nearby small creature after a difficulty 2 outdoor-survival task; those within short range will not harm the druid or designated allies until a recovery of at least ten minutes. It cannot affect hostile swarms of level 3 or higher, and Effort can make the creatures act as an NPC ally.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Druid Abilities — Friend to Small Creatures (cypher-rd#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to peaceful influence over one nearby small-creature type until recovery; a world can widen the target or command more strongly, because hostile or powerful creatures resist control.

rules.statement: Divine Radiance can bless a short-range target so they gain an asset to one action before their next recovery of at least ten minutes; Effort adds two targets. Alternatively, it attacks up to five nearby undead of level 2 or less, which flee for their next turn; Effort adds two targets and raises the level limit by 1, and at tier 3 the effect can instead prevent actions for one turn.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Cleric Abilities — Divine Radiance (cypher-rd#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a single brief blessing or a limited undead repulse; a world can turn up targets or incapacitation, because greater divine influence costs effort.

rules.statement: When a druid’s seed attack hits, it deals 3 damage and sets the target on fire for 1 damage per round until the target spends an action extinguishing it or the druid next recovers.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Druid Abilities — Seeds of Fury (cypher-rd#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to 3 initial damage and 1 recurring damage; a world can adjust the burn’s intensity or duration, because the flames persist only briefly unless actively doused.

rules.statement: Overwatch lets an archer attack a viable target entering a chosen limited area, ignoring benefits from cover, position, surprise, range, illumination, or visibility; the attack deals 1 extra damage. The archer may maintain the setup as long as reasonable.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Archer Abilities — Overwatch (cypher-rd#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one watched area and one triggered shot; a world can widen the area or limit duration, because maintaining vigilance and a ready weapon is demanding.

rules.statement: Swords-and-sorcery wound treatment takes 1 minute for a minor wound, 10 minutes for a moderate wound, and 1 hour for a major wound.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Swords & Sorcery — Wound Treatment (cypher-rd#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to progressively longer treatment for worse wounds; a world can change these times, because severe injuries require more sustained care.

rules.statement: Axe Hook can trade 2 damage for making a target drop a weapon or shield, which they must spend an action to retrieve; alternatively, it trades 1 damage to hinder the target’s tasks until the attacker’s next turn.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Axe Hook (cypher-rd#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to letting a successful weapon attack impose a brief disarm or hindrance; a world can make recovery harder or easier depending on how exposed the dropped gear is.

rules.statement: Split Skull, Gut Ripper, and Swing Through each raise the attack’s GM intrusion range from a roll of 1 to rolls of 1–3. On a hit, each offers a choice of extra damage or another effect; their intrusions can damage the attacker or impair, dislodge, or break the weapon.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Split Skull; Gut Ripper; Swing Through (cypher-rd#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a stronger attack with a wider chance of mishap; a world can vary the consequences, with weapon trouble and self-injury as the cost.

rules.statement: An idol made in a ten-minute ritual lasts until its magic is exhausted and grants one selected benefit to anyone who prays to it as an action. Each use has a 1–2 depletion result on a d6; carrying the idol requires Effort.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Priest Abilities — Idol (cypher-rd#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a reusable, placed blessing with a chance of depletion per use; a world can make the idol portable by charging Effort, or restrict its placement to protected solid surfaces.

rules.statement: The idol’s bestial-fury benefit changes the supplicant visibly, prevents Intellect spending except to regain composure, and makes them attack every living creature within short range, rolling twice and taking the better result. It ends after a ten-minute recovery or a successful difficulty 2 Intellect task, then inflicts two moderate wounds; a furious NPC is one level higher and takes 6 damage when it ends.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Priest Abilities — Idol: Bestial Fury (cypher-rd#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a potent, uncontrolled combat state that exacts a substantial physical toll; a world can change the trigger or recovery method, but the supplicant risks harming allies and self.

rules.statement: Opening the sorcerer’s inner eye takes a ten-minute ritual and a blade puncture that causes a minor wound; it lasts until a ten-hour recovery. While open, physical perception tasks are hindered, but the sorcerer can use the listed spirit-sensing and mind-affecting abilities; from tier 3, activation takes one minute and the perception hindrance is removed.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Sorcerer Abilities — Open Inner Eye (cypher-rd#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to enhanced supernatural perception and mental powers in exchange for a lasting wound and impaired ordinary perception; a world can ease activation at higher tier while retaining the bodily price.

rules.statement: A successful Sorcerous Suggestion makes a target with a mind attempt one specified simple action on their next turn, such as answering a prompt, manipulating an object, moving an immediate distance, or staying still.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Sorcerer Abilities — Sorcerous Suggestion (cypher-rd#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one brief, limited compelled action after a successful attack; a world can broaden or narrow the permitted actions, with mindless creatures remaining outside the effect.

rules.statement: A Witch can brew a potion in ten minutes by choosing a manifest cypher effect. The potion counts against the brewer’s or recipient’s cypher limit, displacing one current cypher if necessary; higher tiers allow medium effects at tier 3 and advanced effects at tier 6, while Potion Cyphers permits two extra created potions to be carried.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Witch Abilities — Brew Potion; Potion Cyphers (cypher-rd#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to making a chosen magical effect portable but subject to cypher capacity; a world can expand the available potency by tier, while excess potions force the loss of another cypher’s magic.

rules.statement: In epic fantasy, treating a minor wound takes 10 minutes, a moderate wound takes 1 hour, and a major wound takes 1 week. Manifest cyphers are rare in this setting, and genre abilities are gained at tiers 3 and 6, with one mid-tier ability replaceable at tier 6.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Epic Fantasy — Wound Treatment; Manifest Cyphers; Genre Abilities (cypher-rd#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to slow recovery and scarce temporary magic to emphasize serious consequences; a world can shorten treatment or increase cypher frequency to make play less demanding.

rules.statement: A character can take three additional minor wounds and one additional moderate wound; the Swashbuckler and Warrior also gain +3 in their main combat Pool, while the Wizard gains +3 Intellect and +1 Might. Each of these types gains +1 Edge in a chosen Pool and may use the weapons and armor specified for the type without restriction.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Swashbuckler Abilities; Warrior Abilities; Wizard Abilities (cypher-rd#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to these fixed type benefits; a world can change wound and Pool bonuses to tune resilience or specialization, reflecting how its training shapes characters.

rules.statement: A Swashbuckler may spend 1 Speed when attacking to accept a GM intrusion range increased by 2 (from a roll of 1 to rolls of 1–3 on a d20); on a hit, choose either +2 damage or deal 1 less damage and make the foe drop an item held in one hand, which takes an action to retrieve.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Swashbuckler Abilities — Flamboyant Swordplay (cypher-rd#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the listed risk and benefits; a world can change the intrusion range or effect strength, with showy combat inviting mishaps.

rules.statement: A Wizard can spend 2 Intellect to prepare a low-power manifest cypher as a lasting spell after ten minutes; casting it takes an action and 2 Intellect, does not count against the cypher limit, and does not consume the spell. A ten-hour recovery allows a different choice and ends durations of the previous spell; at tiers 3 and 6, the available power and casting cost rise to medium/4 Intellect and advanced/6 Intellect.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Wizard Abilities — Prepare Spell (cypher-rd#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one prepared cypher-spell at a time, with tier-based access; a world can vary preparation slots or cost, reflecting the difficulty of sustaining learned magic.

rules.statement: A creature designated within immediate range can reduce wound severity from a chosen energy type by one step until it takes a one-hour or longer recovery; spending Effort reduces severity by another step. Each protected creature’s duration ends independently.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Mid-Tier Fantasy Abilities — Elemental Protection (cypher-rd#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one-step protection for a group until recovery; a world can change the area or severity reduction, reflecting how much magical shelter it can provide.

rules.statement: Invisibility lasts until the user reveals their presence or position, or takes a ten-minute or longer recovery. While invisible, the user’s attacks are eased by two steps and attacks against them are hindered by four steps, or are nearly impossible if the attacker cannot locate them; Effort can instead make a touched creature invisible.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: High-Tier Fantasy Abilities — Invisibility (cypher-rd#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the stated visibility-ending actions and combat modifiers; a world can broaden or narrow what reveals the user, reflecting how fragile concealment is.

rules.statement: A portal made within long range connects to a location the caster can see or knows exists; it admits the caster and creatures no larger than them, and anything entering immediately emerges at the other end. It remains open until a ten-minute or longer recovery.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: High-Tier Fantasy Abilities — Magic Portal (cypher-rd#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a two-way traversable opening that persists until recovery; a world can restrict destination knowledge, size, or duration, reflecting the hazards of crossing space.

rules.statement: A body’s appearance and carried or worn items can be changed to resemble someone else, without changing any statistics; the disguise lasts up to a day or ends when the user takes an action to revert. Close scrutiny eases disguise tasks by three steps.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: High-Tier Fantasy Abilities — Mask (cypher-rd#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a day-long cosmetic transformation with unchanged capabilities; a world can shorten duration or limit copied details, reflecting the effort needed to sustain a convincing disguise.

rules.statement: A successful Intellect attack can end one ongoing magical effect within immediate range; against a cypher or magical device, success instead prevents it from functioning until a ten-minute or longer recovery. Effort lets the user attempt this defensively in response to an attack on another creature’s turn.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: High-Tier Fantasy Abilities — Spellbreaker (cypher-rd#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to ending one nearby magical effect on success; a world can limit eligible effects or allow defensive use, reflecting how readily magic can be disrupted.

rules.statement: When a rule sets a minimum result, a roll below that minimum is treated as the minimum; spending Effort can raise the minimum by 3, and some abilities improve their minimum at tier 3. The stated abilities that use this rule cost 1–3 Pool points, as specified in their descriptions.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Engineer Abilities; Operative Abilities; Pilot Abilities; Soldier Abilities; Android Abilities; Scoundrel Abilities (cypher-rd#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the listed minimums and costs; a world can adjust the minimum or Effort surcharge to represent how reliable trained specialists are.

rules.statement: A successful engineering task at difficulty equal to a device’s level plus 1 temporarily restores a broken device or inactive power source for a few uses. A full repair usually takes at least days, special tools and parts, and resource points.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Engineer Abilities—Repair (cypher-rd#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to short-lived repairs with a full repair taking days and resources; a world can change the repair window to reflect how scarce parts and tools are.

rules.statement: A successful difficulty 3 engineering task can raise a device to about 25 percent above its rated performance, but after the user’s next ten-hour recovery it breaks and needs a full repair. A repaired or upgraded device depletes on a 1–6 result on a d20 per use, improving to 1–2 at tier 3; the process takes ten minutes and requires suitable tools and parts.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Engineer Abilities—Modify Device (cypher-rd#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a temporary performance boost with a per-use breakdown chance; a world can adjust the depletion range to make improvised engineering safer or riskier.

rules.statement: A medic can prepare a medical device as an attack against an adjacent creature; the eased attack prevents that creature from acting on its next turn. Spending two Effort levels instead makes the target unconscious until the medic uses a recovery; preparing the medicine and attacking each take an action.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Medic Abilities—Bad Medicine (cypher-rd#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one lost turn or unconsciousness until recovery; a world can alter the duration or access to medical supplies to set how disabling misuse of medicine is.

rules.statement: When an operative rolls below 6 to pass as a generic member of a category, treat the result as 6; Effort raises that minimum by 3, and at tier 3 the minimum is 12. The successful disguise of identity lasts until a ten-minute recovery or until circumstances expose the operative, and it cannot imitate a specific person.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Operative Abilities—Spin Identity (cypher-rd#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to generic identities lasting until recovery; a world can shorten or lengthen persistence according to how pervasive identity checks are.

rules.statement: A psion can read a visible creature’s surface thoughts at short range, making an Intellect attack if the creature resists; after contact, reading lasts until the psion takes a ten-minute recovery. The ability costs 2 Intellect and takes an action.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Psion Abilities—Mind Reading (cypher-rd#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to surface thoughts and a recovery-limited connection; a world can make contact easier or harder depending on how guarded minds are.

rules.statement: A psion can distort their appearance until a ten-minute recovery, easing their dodge and Intellect defense rolls; the distortion also reduces incoming mental wound severity by one step. The ability costs 1 Intellect.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Psion Abilities—Psychic Veil (cypher-rd#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a persistent defensive veil with one-step severity reduction; a world can tune its duration or protection to reflect the prevalence of psychic threats.

rules.statement: An android needs engineering rather than healing to remove wounds: repair difficulty is level 1 for minor, level 3 for moderate, and level 5 for major wounds. Without a suitable power supply during a ten-hour recovery, the android loses its normal one-action recovery and its bonus power-connected recovery.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Android Abilities—Machine Not Flesh (cypher-rd#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to wound repair and power-dependent recovery as written; a world can relax the power requirement or raise repair difficulties to change android resilience.

rules.statement: A soldier can make an additional attack as an extra action after attacking by activating a combat implant, but doing so inflicts a moderate wound on the soldier.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Soldier Abilities—Push Implant (cypher-rd#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one extra attack at the cost of a moderate wound; a world can change the wound cost to reflect how dangerous combat implants are.

rules.statement: Redline Maneuver costs 1 Speed or Intellect and raises the GM intrusion range by 2; on a successful piloting task of difficulty 2 or higher, it permits an unusually risky starcraft maneuver.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Starpilot Abilities — Redline Maneuver (cypher-rd#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to difficulty 2 and +2 intrusion range; the GM can raise the difficulty for more extreme maneuvers, reflecting the risk of craft damage or failure.

rules.statement: A device made with Always Tinkering takes 10 minutes, is single-use, and counts against its bearer’s cypher limit; if that limit is already full, one existing cypher must be sacrificed or displaced. Its available effects expand at tiers 3 and 6.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Tech Abilities — Always Tinkering (cypher-rd#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a single-use device that occupies a cypher slot; a world can restrict available device effects to reflect its technology.

rules.statement: Craft Device costs 5 or more Intellect and an hour, and requires success at a difficulty 3 engineering task. Its small, fragile product uses a selected low-power manifest-cypher effect, does not count against a cypher limit, and depletes on 1 in 1d6; higher-tier effects require Effort.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Tech Abilities — Craft Device (cypher-rd#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a portable but fragile device with a 1-in-1d6 depletion chance; a world can change the effect tier or reliability to match available technology.

rules.statement: Smooth Operator reduces an expensive item’s price to a moderately priced item’s price; Effort allows further price reductions. It works only where goods and services are routinely traded and renews after reaching a new market or waiting at least a month; at tier 3 it can be used twice before renewal.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Trader Abilities — Smooth Operator (cypher-rd#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one discount per market per month; a world can alter the renewal interval, with access to markets determining how often the benefit returns.

rules.statement: After a successful positive social interaction or Fast Talk, if the other creature turns hostile within about a day, the Dealer reduces the severity of its first successful attack by one step; at tier 3, that attack instead causes no damage.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Dealer Abilities — When the Deal Bombs (cypher-rd#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one protected first hit within about a day; a world can adjust the window or protection, with the benefit arising from the earlier deal.

rules.statement: In a postapocalypse setting, removing a minor wound by treatment takes 10 minutes, a moderate wound takes one hour, and a major wound takes one week. A Tender with a scavenged doctor’s bag can halve treatment time or treat twice as many wounds for one character in the usual time.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Postapocalypse — Wound Treatment; Tender Abilities — Wasteland Healer (cypher-rd#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the listed recovery times and the Tender’s choice of faster or broader treatment; a world can change the duration to reflect how scarce effective care is.

rules.statement: A scavenged doctor’s bag depletes on 1 in 1d10; a Tender can restock it by spending at least an hour searching inhabited ruins and 1 resource point.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Tender Equipment Bundle (cypher-rd#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a 1-in-1d10 depletion chance and a one-hour, one-resource restock; a world can change the scarcity or recovery cost of medical supplies.

rules.statement: The listed science-fiction abilities are gated by character tier: characters gain a mid-tier ability at tier 3 and a high-tier ability at tier 6, and at tier 6 may exchange one mid-tier choice for another. The GM may disallow choices that do not fit the campaign.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Science Fiction Genre Abilities (cypher-rd#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to choices at tiers 3 and 6 with one tier-6 mid-tier exchange; a world can restrict options to preserve its technological assumptions.

rules.statement: A Human character may choose a second descriptor and add its benefits to the regular descriptor; a character whose type represents their species instead gains the benefit of two descriptors when other characters use the standard species options.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Human; Species or Type? (cypher-rd#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to granting the extra descriptor benefits; a setting can restrict this option to mixed-species groups to keep species choices distinct.

rules.statement: A Mutant ignores the GM intrusion normally triggered by rolling 1 on a Might defense task and adapts any tier 1 focus ability into a mutation, subject to GM agreement.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Mutant (cypher-rd#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one adapted tier 1 ability and immunity to this specific intrusion; a world can limit mutation choices to fit its biology and balance.

rules.statement: A Naron can telepathically communicate at short range with intelligent creatures without making vocal sounds, but cannot read thoughts or communicate with a creature that refuses contact.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Naron (cypher-rd#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to willing, short-range mental conversation; a world can broaden targets or range, with privacy and mental resistance as limits.

rules.statement: A Prota can reshape its body over about 10 minutes into an evocative but not exact imitation; for a task specifically suited to the new shape it gains an asset, and it can take one extra minor wound.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Prota (cypher-rd#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to task-specific body shaping after 10 minutes; a world can expand the forms or shorten the time, balanced by the inability to copy things exactly.

rules.statement: Superhero power shifts act as permanent free Effort for designated tasks, do not count against the Effort maximum, and are capped at three shifts per category. A shift to ability damage adds +3 damage; other shifts affect their listed task categories.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Power Shifts (cypher-rd#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to permanent, category-limited bonuses of at most three shifts; a world can change the cap or bonus size to set the superheroes' power level.

rules.statement: A Flight shift permits flight at ordinary human running speed, with limited maneuverability, and lets the character carry one creature of their size or smaller. A Healing shift grants one extra one-action recovery per day; Increased Range moves an ability up one range band; Prodigy exchanges one tier 1 ability for a tier 2 focus ability or two tier 1 abilities for a tier 3 focus ability.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Power Shifts (cypher-rd#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the stated narrow benefits and daily recovery limit; a world can increase mobility, range, or ability access at the cost of broader balance.

rules.statement: A superhero can rally a major wound by taking an action and spending 10 Might. Treating wounds takes one Last action for a minor wound, one minute for a moderate wound, and ten minutes for a major wound.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Playing a Superhero Character (cypher-rd#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to these recovery costs and times; a world can make treatment slower or more resource-intensive to emphasize danger.

rules.statement: For tasks using a chosen Pool, Superheroics adds the character's rank to the maximum Effort they can apply; the character may instead take a moderate wound to gain two free Effort levels, if that stays within the Pool's Effort limit. Recovery points from the ability go only to the chosen Pool and gain a bonus equal to rank.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Crimefighter Abilities; Superheroics (cypher-rd#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a rank-based Effort increase and a moderate wound for the optional boost; a world can change the wound cost or Effort ceiling to tune power.

rules.statement: Superhero task difficulty can reach 15 rather than stopping at 10; each level above 10 represents a further step beyond ordinary impossibility. Superheroes can also exceed the usual six levels of Effort through Superheroics.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Really Impossible Tasks (cypher-rd#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a difficulty cap of 15 and permit Superheroics to exceed six Effort levels; a setting can lower either limit to make extraordinary feats rarer.

rules.statement: A character chooses two tier 1 abilities from a focus, then one ability at each later tier. Later choices must be at the character’s tier or lower and connected to an ability already chosen; an ability that modifies another requires the character to have that earlier ability.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Focus Abilities (cypher-rd#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to connected, tier-limited ability choices; a world can loosen the links to allow broader development, at the cost of less distinct progression.

rules.statement: Superheroics adds the character’s rank to the Effort they can apply on tasks using one chosen Pool, and adds that rank to recovery points placed in that Pool. The character may take a moderate wound to gain two free Effort levels for such a task, without exceeding their Effort limit.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Living God Abilities (cypher-rd#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to rank-based Effort and recovery bonuses with a wound traded for extra Effort; a world can change the wound cost or cap to tune the power of heroic exertion.

rules.statement: A duplicate lasts until a ten-minute recovery, dismissal, reuse of the ability, or its death. Only one normally exists at once; each duplicate’s death gives its creator a moderate wound, and its copied equipment disappears with it unless acquired separately.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Origin Superhero Abilities — Duplicate (cypher-rd#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one temporary duplicate and a moderate wound on its death; a world can alter the number or the creator’s cost, with more duplicates making replication less risky.

rules.statement: A focus’s shroud of flame persists until a ten-minute recovery, harms creatures that touch or strike its user for 2 damage, and reduces flame or heat wound severity by one step. Its user can also make a light unarmed attack that deals 2 fire damage.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Blazes With Fire — Shroud of Flame (cypher-rd#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to persistent personal fire protection with contact damage; a world can change its duration or damage to make the shroud safer or more hazardous.

rules.statement: Stone Body means its user needs no food, drink, or air, can take two extra minor wounds, eases block tasks, and deals 2 extra damage with unarmed attacks. Its mineral stiffness makes dodge tasks an inability.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Abides in Stone — Stone Body (cypher-rd#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to durability and strength offset by poor dodging; a world can adjust the physical drawbacks to reflect how flexible mineral bodies are.

rules.statement: When a character uses Still As a Statue, they cannot move, take physical actions, or sense their surroundings, and time seems not to pass for them. After 24 hours they wake and remove three wounds of any severity; an ally can wake them earlier by spending at least 2 Might, but then no wounds are removed.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Abides in Stone — Still As a Statue (cypher-rd#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a 24-hour inert recovery that heals three wounds, with an ally able to end it early for at least 2 Might; a world can change the healing or interruption cost.

rules.statement: An automaton follower can be repaired by its builder: the level 2 assistant regains 2 health after a few minutes of attention, and if destroyed can be restored by spending resources and several days tinkering. Gaining resource points also grants the builder one extra point restricted to crafting or repairs.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Builds Allies — Automaton Assistant; Efficient Builder (cypher-rd#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to time and resource costs for restoring constructs, with one bonus crafting-only point per resource gain; a world can raise those costs to make construct upkeep more demanding.

rules.statement: A command effect can force a machine to take one action within its capabilities on its next turn; if that action would directly harm it or its allies, the attack to command it is hindered. Some controlled intelligent machines may become hostile afterward.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Quick Control (cypher-rd#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one forced action with a harm-related difficulty increase; a world could relax the limit, at the cost of making machine control easier to abuse.

rules.statement: A prepared spell is selected from a low-power manifest cypher after 10 minutes, costs 2 Intellect to cast, persists after casting, and can be changed after a 10-hour recovery; changing it ends the old spell’s ongoing durations. At tiers 3 and 6, medium- and advanced-power options cost 4 and 6 Intellect respectively.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Casts Spells — Prepare Spell (cypher-rd#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one daily prepared effect that is reusable but costs Intellect; a world could permit more preparations, at the cost of greater versatility.

rules.statement: An animal transformation can last until a recovery and grants animal movement and a minor animal ability, but makes equipment unusable and hinders tasks requiring hands; effort can permit speech, a hybrid form, or a creature-related skill asset.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Changes Shape — Animal Shape (cypher-rd#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to animal traits with practical limits on gear, speech, and hand use; a world could remove those limits, at the cost of making transformation broadly superior.

rules.statement: Telepathic contact may be limited by willingness, range, and duration; mental control instead requires a successful attack, touch, and a target of level 2 or lower, and ends at a 10-minute recovery. A controlled target forgets the control and its actions when the effect ends.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Commands Mental Powers — Telepathic; Mind Control (cypher-rd#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to constrained mental links and short-lived control with memory loss; a world could lengthen control, at the cost of stronger consent and autonomy concerns.

rules.statement: An animated corpse follows verbal commands until a one-hour recovery, then becomes inert; it can be animated again. More powerful animation raises the follower’s level and the Intellect cost for each additional body.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Consorts With the Dead — Basic, Greater, and True Necromancy (cypher-rd#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to temporary animated bodies without their former memories or abilities; a world could grant them more agency, at the cost of less reliable obedience.

rules.statement: A beast companion is a follower, and a dead companion can be replaced through several days of searching and befriending; a mount takes about a week to replace. Some abilities instead influence nearby small creatures or plants, with stronger command requiring effort.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Controls Beasts — Beast Companion; Friend to Small Creatures; Mount (cypher-rd#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a small, replaceable roster of bonded followers and limited influence over local creatures; a world could allow larger groups, at the cost of greater upkeep and attention.

rules.statement: A level 5 force field protects its automaton and creatures within immediate range until a 10-minute recovery; protected creatures reduce incoming wounds by one severity, while NPCs take 3 less damage.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Tier 5 — Automaton Force Field Upgrade (cypher-rd#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a local protective field with a recovery-based end condition; a world could extend its duration, at the cost of making safe zones easier to maintain.

rules.statement: When the shapeshifter would die, they instead fall unconscious for one round, then recover 1d6 + 6 Pool points and remove one moderate and one major wound; their tasks are hindered until a 10-hour recovery, and a second death before then is final.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Changes Shape — Not Dead Yet (cypher-rd#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one costly reprieve before recovery; a world could allow repeated returns, at the cost of imposing a larger or accumulating penalty.

rules.statement: Beast Call spends 5 Intellect to summon one level 4 beast or a horde that collectively functions as a level 4 creature. The creatures obey only while the user focuses and spends an action directing them each turn; they must be local and able to reach the summoner themselves.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Beast Call (cypher-rd#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a temporary, locally available companion that requires ongoing attention; a world can permit remote arrivals by changing the native-and-travel limitation, at the cost of weakening the place-based constraint.

rules.statement: Illusions made by Minor Illusion and Major Illusion last until the creator takes a ten-minute recovery; they vanish sooner if the creator moves beyond the specified range. Major changes to a minor image require renewed concentration, while the major scene can change as directed without it.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Crafts Illusions, Tier 1–3 (cypher-rd#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to recovery-bounded images that fail outside their range; a world can extend duration or remove the range limit, at the cost of making deception easier to sustain.

rules.statement: Move Metal can exert hand-like force on metal within short range, but cannot provide fine control or move an object beyond what the user could physically manage. Affecting an unwilling creature or its gear requires an Intellect attack; disrupting nearby electronics hinders them by two steps for one round.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Employs Magnetism, Tier 1 (cypher-rd#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to limited remote manipulation rather than precise telekinesis; a world can allow finer or stronger control, at the cost of removing the physical-hand constraint.

rules.statement: Electromagnetically Charge heals one wound severity or restores a mundane handheld electrical device’s charge. Each use before a recovery costs one more Intellect point than the previous use, beginning at 1, and a recovery resets the cost to 1.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Employs Magnetism, Tier 2 (cypher-rd#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a repeat-use cost that escalates until recovery; a world can keep the cost fixed, at the cost of making repeated healing or device charging easier.

rules.statement: Magnetic Field grounds incoming ranged metallic projectiles and disperses attacks in the electromagnetic spectrum, making the user immune to them for one round. The user must be aware of the attack to stop it.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Employs Magnetism, Tier 4 (cypher-rd#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a brief defensive field that works only against specified attacks the user notices; a world can broaden its coverage, at the cost of reducing the importance of awareness and attack type.

rules.statement: Inspiring Ease gives allies who share a ten-hour recovery with the entertainer one task-easing use per day while they remain within long range. The effect is suspended beyond that distance and ends if the entertainer takes a ten-hour recovery away from them.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Entertains, Tier 2 (cypher-rd#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a daily benefit sustained by proximity and shared rest; a world can make inspiration persist at any distance, at the cost of removing its social and positional limits.

rules.statement: One With the Wild affects the user and allies within long range until an hour-long recovery: local natural animals and plants will not knowingly harm them, their three Edges each rise by 1, and their recoveries restore twice as many points.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Explores, Tier 6 (cypher-rd#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a temporary bounded wilderness benefit with several linked effects; a world can extend it beyond the wild or make it permanent, at the cost of its location and duration constraints.

rules.statement: When a character is attacked while using Taunting Defense, the foe’s attack is hindered; if it hits, it inflicts an additional minor wound.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Fights With Panache, Tier 1 (cypher-rd#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to trading a harder incoming attack for worse consequences on a hit; a world can remove the added wound, at the cost of making the defensive taunt safer.

rules.statement: The HUD improves vision in darkness and through obscurants. With one Effort it can see 5 miles and through level 4 basic material for two rounds; with two Effort it can see through level 4 special material for two rounds, and a successful Intellect task extends this to level 5 or higher.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: HUD (0+ Intellect) (cypher-rd#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to short-range sensing through limited material; a world can raise the material threshold at the cost of Effort and a successful task.

rules.statement: Deep Reserves transfers up to 6 points among Pools, at one point per round, and refreshes after a ten-hour recovery. Fusion lets the character use fused manifest cyphers and artifacts as First actions; fusing or detaching takes an action.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Tier 4, Deep Reserves; Fusion (cypher-rd#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to slow, limited resource transfer and faster use of body-bound devices; a world can raise the cap or speed by increasing the cost.

rules.statement: A machine contact requires a willing, able machine within range and lasts until a ten-minute recovery; tasks involving it take half the time, and actions become First actions. Effort can extend the contact to a one-hour recovery and increase range by one step.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Fuses Mind and Machine, Tier 1, Wireless Interface (cypher-rd#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to temporary communication with willing machines; a world can extend range and duration by spending Effort.

rules.statement: Brainwashing controls a touched creature of level 3 or lower after a successful Intellect attack, lasting until a ten-minute recovery; the target forgets the control and its actions afterward. Effort raises the maximum affected level by one.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Infiltrates, Tier 6, Brainwashing (cypher-rd#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to short-lived control of weak targets with erased recollection; a world can permit stronger targets at increasing Intellect cost.

rules.statement: Enlarge lasts until a recovery, increases Might Edge by 1, lets the character ignore the first moderate wound, and makes unarmed attacks deal 4 damage, but hinders dodging. Each use costs one more Might than the previous use until a recovery resets the cost; larger forms replace, rather than stack with, smaller-form benefits.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Grows to Towering Heights, Tier 1, Enlarge (cypher-rd#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to temporary growth with a rising repeated-use cost; a world can allow larger forms by charging additional Might and imposing defensive drawbacks.

rules.statement: Beast Form occurs involuntarily on five consecutive nights each month and lasts until dawn’s first hint or moonset. In that form the character attacks every living creature within short range and cannot spend Intellect except to attempt a difficulty 4 return to normal; afterward tasks are hindered, more severely and longer if no substantial creature was killed and eaten.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Howls at the Moon, Tier 1, Beast Form (cypher-rd#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a powerful but dangerous scheduled transformation; a world can reduce loss of control through abilities that make changing voluntary or easier.

rules.statement: Quarry selects one visible creature and grants an asset on tasks involving pursuit, understanding, interaction, attack, or defense against it; only one quarry can be active. Multiple Quarries permits four visible targets, with each additional target increasing the cost by 2 Intellect.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Hunts, Tier 2, Quarry; Tier 6, Multiple Quarries (cypher-rd#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a single designated target that improves relevant actions; a world can broaden the target set at additional Intellect cost.

rules.statement: A follower or ally within short range can receive a command that makes their next action a First action, except a normally Last action remains so; this ability cannot be used again before a ten-minute recovery.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Leads, Tier 1, Lighting a Fire Under Them (cypher-rd#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one accelerated action for a nearby ally per recovery interval; a world can allow repeated commands by shortening the refresh period or changing the limitation.

rules.statement: Telekinesis affects a visible object within long range if it is no heavier than the user could handle by hand; it can move or manipulate it over one round, or hinder a creature through a successful attack. Reshape changes material only within a 5-foot cube, with complex work requiring ten minutes and a successful hindered crafting task.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Masters Telekinesis, Tier 1, Telekinesis; Tier 6, Reshape (cypher-rd#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to limited remote manipulation and shape changes that preserve material; a world can permit heavier or more complex effects by raising task difficulty and time.

rules.statement: An ability that sets a minimum roll treats any lower result as that minimum; spending Effort can raise the minimum by 3, and some abilities raise it again at tier 3. This does not make an impossible action succeed.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Perfect Attack; Escape; Naturally Strong; Natural Sneak (cypher-rd#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to raising low rolls without making impossible tasks possible; worlds can change the floor or Effort cost to tune reliability, since extraordinary training carries a resource cost.

rules.statement: Several attacks and defenses can prevent harm without an ordinary defense roll, but commonly impose a cost such as hindering later actions, reducing damage, or consuming ammunition. Some effects still inflict reduced damage on a failed attack.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Shot Collision; Spray; Supreme Retribution (cypher-rd#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to allowing specified defensive or area effects with their stated action and resource costs; a world can make them more reliable or more costly, because protection and collateral damage are consequential.

rules.statement: Some abilities persist until the user takes a recovery, while others end when the affected target acts to counter them, or when the user spends a specified later action. Persistent effects can therefore be bounded by recovery or by a counteraction.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Tier 1, Rides the Lightning; Tier 2, Quells Evil (cypher-rd#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the passage's stated recovery or counteraction limit; worlds can shorten or extend duration, with longer-lasting effects granting greater leverage.

rules.statement: Some powers require a successful attack or task against each target separately; others affect targets automatically, sometimes with a reduced effect even on a failed roll. Effort can raise target limits, damage, or the maximum level of creature affected where specified.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Tier 1, Quells Evil; Tier 4, Rides the Lightning (cypher-rd#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to individual checks and explicit target caps; a world can broaden targets or remove checks by increasing cost or reducing potency, because affecting many creatures is a strong advantage.

rules.statement: The supernatural-force discipline allows telekinetic movement and manipulation at a distance, limited by sight, range, weight, and task or attack success; some actions take a full round to complete.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Tier 2, Reveres a Supernatural Force (cypher-rd#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to visible, range- and weight-limited manipulation that takes time; worlds can loosen those limits, with greater reach or force demanding greater expenditure.

rules.statement: Lightning abilities can move a user rapidly between visible or familiar locations, but travel is limited by barriers, planet, or access to the open sky depending on the ability.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Bolt Rider; Flash Across the Miles (cypher-rd#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the stated line-of-sight, barrier, and destination restrictions; worlds can permit more destinations at higher cost, since rapid travel bypasses ordinary obstacles.

rules.statement: A creature affected by a successful rebuke follows the user's specified goal, even if that goal risks harm to itself or allies; the control persists until the user's next ten-minute recovery.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Rebuke Evil (cypher-rd#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one successfully targeted creature and a recovery-bounded command; worlds can allow more targets or longer control, at the cost of greater effort or risk.

rules.statement: Some abilities change wounds or restore resources: resilience can reduce a fall or poison wound by one severity step, while recovery effects may restore pools or remove wounds, sometimes with a delayed penalty or a limit before recovery.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Safe Fall; Wilderness Experience; Not Dead Yet (cypher-rd#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the passage's fixed recovery and wound limits; worlds can make healing stronger or more frequent, balanced by exhaustion, hindrance, or a recovery requirement.

rules.statement: Natural foliage can hold a foe in place and hinder physical tasks until the user takes a recovery of at least ten minutes; the user can keep restraining a foe who tries to escape with another Intellect roll. The same power can clear entangling plants from an immediate area.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Nature’s Grip (cypher-rd#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a held target that cannot move and is hindered; a world can vary what counts as natural foliage or how long it holds, because the effect draws on local plant life.

rules.statement: A beast that can see and hear the user can be calmed until the user takes a ten-minute recovery, or only while the user spends actions calming it. Each additional beast costs 2 Intellect; aliens, extradimensional beings, very intelligent creatures, and robots are excluded.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Nature’s Voice (cypher-rd#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to calming ordinary nonhuman beasts within long range; a world can broaden or narrow the definition of beast, reflecting its ecology and the power’s limits.

rules.statement: Some abilities remain active until a specified recovery, while others need continuing concentration or actions; ending the duration may also impose a recovery penalty. For example, Moon Shape lasts until an hour recovery, and reverting voluntarily is a difficulty 2 Intellect task.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Moon Shape; various ability entries (cypher-rd#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the duration and recovery stated for each effect; a world can change those durations, with longer transformations or control requiring greater lingering costs.

rules.statement: A character’s abilities can create or control persistent hazards and barriers: the weapon wall blocks an immediate area while maintained, and crossing it deals 10 damage; the storm lasts until a ten-minute recovery and can strike for 4 damage per action.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Weave an Iron Wall; Call the Storm (cypher-rd#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a maintained barrier or persistent storm with the listed effect; a world can adjust area and damage, with broad coverage making the wielder spend actions to sustain it.

rules.statement: Abilities can alter machines at range or through an accessible network, but security makes remote hacking harder and machine control can be resisted by the target’s level. Some effects persist only while the user concentrates; others last until a recovery.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Talks to Machines; Control Electric Device; Machine Control (cypher-rd#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to control limited by network access, security, and the machine’s level; a world can change connectivity and machine autonomy, with stronger safeguards restricting remote influence.

rules.statement: A touch can reduce wound severity, cure maladies, or restore the dead if they are otherwise intact and the stated time limit is met. Repeated use of some healing abilities raises their Intellect cost until a recovery resets it.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Tends to the Wounded; Healing Hand; Resuscitate (cypher-rd#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the listed wound changes and death limits, with escalating costs where given; a world can make revival harder or more expensive because death is difficult to reverse.

rules.statement: Time can be rewound a few seconds so a creature may redo its last action, without remembering the original action; using this ability renews only after a recovery.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Rewind Time (cypher-rd#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one creature redoing its immediately prior action; a world can change the window or number of uses, since rewriting events risks disrupting causality.

rules.statement: Phasing can let a character pass through physical barriers of level 5 or less at 1 foot per round, but not energy barriers; more powerful barriers require Effort. A phased character may also become wholly unable to affect or be affected by ordinary matter and energy, at the cost of being unable to act physically on it.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Walks Through Walls; Untouchable (cypher-rd#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to slow passage through bounded physical barriers and temporary intangibility; a world can change barrier limits or duration, with greater phase depth risking loss or displacement.

rules.statement: Armor eases blocking by 1 step for light, 2 for medium, and 3 for heavy armor, while hindering dodging by the same number of steps. If the wearer cannot use that armor freely, its dodge penalty also hinders all Speed tasks; damaged armor loses 1 step of its block benefit but keeps its normal dodge penalty.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Armor (cypher-rd#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to these category-based block benefits and dodge penalties; a setting can change armor’s effectiveness, with damage reducing protection.

rules.statement: Light weapons deal 2 damage and ease attacks; medium weapons deal 4 damage; heavy weapons deal 6 damage and require two hands. A light weapon can be used as a First action, while a heavy weapon is a Last action; unfamiliar weapons hinder the attack.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Weapons (cypher-rd#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to fixed damage and timing by weapon class; a world can change access to weapon training, with unfamiliarity imposing a penalty.

rules.statement: Explosives can affect multiple creatures in an area, with a separate attack roll against each target unless the GM chooses one roll for all. A failed attack usually still deals 1 damage; each Effort level adds 2 damage, and player characters in the area defend with a block or dodge roll.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Explosive Weapons (cypher-rd#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to area attacks with reduced damage on a miss; a world can change the blast’s area or severity, at the cost of greater danger to everyone nearby.

rules.statement: Cyphers are single-use effects, normally level 4, and usually affect one task unless a duration is specified. They take no action to activate; an ongoing effect that lasts until a recovery can instead be ended early as an extra action at no cost.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Cyphers — Reading a Cypher Description (cypher-rd#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one use and one task; a world can allow longer effects, balanced by an explicit duration or recovery-based endpoint.

rules.statement: Most characters can hold 2 cyphers at a time; a character’s type sets their limit, and some focus or higher-tier abilities raise it. Discarding a cypher as an action frees a slot, and significant rests are a usual opportunity to receive replacements.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Cypher Limit; Gaining New Cyphers (cypher-rd#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a two-cypher capacity and replacement around significant rests; a world can raise the limit, increasing the number of one-use options characters can stockpile.

rules.statement: When an artifact is activated, roll its depletion die; if the result falls in its listed depletion range, it works but this was its final use. An artifact marked with no depletion range never runs out.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Artifacts (cypher-rd#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a depletion roll on each use; a world can make artifacts inexhaustible, removing the risk of losing a powerful item.

rules.statement: A cypher used to help another character grants that character all of the cypher’s assets, and those assets count toward that task’s asset limit. If an unwilling target is to be affected, the user must succeed at an attack roll against them.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Use Them and Replace Them; Reading a Cypher Description (cypher-rd#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to transferring the full task benefit to the assisted character and requiring an attack to affect unwilling targets; a world can relax either limit, making assistance or coercion easier.

rules.statement: A level 3 guard dog attacks and perceives as level 4, but is suited to guarding an area rather than accompanying adventurers into dangerous places; a level 3 riding horse moves a long distance each round, while a level 4 warhorse does likewise.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Fantasy Equipment — Moderately Priced Items; Expensive Items; Very Expensive Items (cypher-rd#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to these stated creature levels and travel capability; a world can permit trained animals to accompany adventurers, exposing them to danger.

rules.statement: A manifest cypher uses your action to activate, and its choices—including the affected roll or target—are made when you use it. To affect an unwilling target, you must succeed at an attack roll against them.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Reading a Manifest Cypher Description (cypher-rd#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default activation takes an action and requires an attack against unwilling targets; a world can make activation faster or more reliable, at the cost of weaker counterplay.

rules.statement: A cypher with no stated duration affects only one task. A cypher that lasts until a recovery ends when you choose to begin that recovery, not after it is completed.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Reading a Manifest Cypher Description (cypher-rd#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default duration is one task unless specified, or until the chosen recovery begins; a world can extend durations, risking more persistent effects.

rules.statement: Your cypher limit counts both nonphysical and manifest cyphers. A physical manifest cypher can be given to an ally or hidden for later, but someone else can find and take a hidden one.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Manifest Cyphers (cypher-rd#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default capacity counts every cypher and physical ones can change hands; a world can raise the limit or restrict transfers, changing scarcity and access.

rules.statement: Manifest cyphers are level 6 effects; for most, level does not change their effect or duration. Some character abilities may interact with a cypher’s level.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Manifest Cypher Power Levels (cypher-rd#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default manifest level is 6 and usually has no mechanical impact; a world can make level matter more, increasing the importance of character abilities that reference it.

rules.statement: A contingent activator links to a manifest cypher you are touching and sets a condition that triggers it. The linked cypher remains usable normally, while the activator occupies capacity until the linked cypher is used, lost, or discarded.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Contingent Activator (cypher-rd#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default triggers are conditional and consume a capacity slot until the linked cypher is gone; a world can loosen either limit, at the cost of more automatic effects or less inventory pressure.

rules.statement: A cluster bomb upgrades another bomb cypher: it gains long range and produces four extra bombs that move a short distance in random directions, then explode next round like the original. The upgrade is expended when used, and no longer counts against capacity.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Cluster Bomb (cypher-rd#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default upgrade adds four delayed, randomly directed blasts and then disappears; a world can change their number or targeting, trading potency for unpredictability.

rules.statement: A cypher that restores a Pool returns 4 points; recovery, wound, duration, and target limits vary by effect. Some task-boosting cyphers provide three assets instead of the usual two, and permit use before or after the roll.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Cypher descriptions (cypher-rd#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default listed values and timing apply, including 4 restored points and three assets where specified; a world can adjust them, balancing reliable boosts against resource pressure.

rules.statement: Several effects require a second action after a successful attack, while others move, hinder, restrain, or incapacitate a target for a stated period. Targets may have escape opportunities, and stronger foes can impose penalties or resist effects.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Cypher descriptions (cypher-rd#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default effects use their listed action costs, resistance, and duration; a world can reduce target resistance or action costs, but risks making control effects dominant.

rules.statement: Most cypher effects last until the named recovery is taken; some instead end after a fixed number of uses, a specific event, or an explicit choice. Effects that end may impose a stated drawback, such as 4 Might or Speed damage after a size change.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Cypher descriptions (cypher-rd#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the stated ending trigger and drawback; a setting can lengthen or shorten duration, with longer effects increasing the power and risk of cyphers.

rules.statement: A power boost cypher modifies one ability chosen when activated, and the user can describe the modification to fit the hero. If no duration is specified, it applies to one task; the GM decides whether these cyphers are available and whether they are physical or nonphysical.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Power Boost Cyphers (cypher-rd#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one chosen ability and one task if no duration is given; a world can limit availability or physical form to control access to ability modification.

rules.statement: A damage-boost cypher adds damage equivalent to two levels of Effort; a source-boost cypher reduces the ability’s Pool cost by 6. Area, range, target-count, and burst boosts instead modify where or how many targets an ability affects, with burst attacks centered on the user at immediate range.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Power Boost Cypher Descriptions (cypher-rd#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the listed numerical bonus and range changes; a world can vary which boost types exist, trading broader effects for balance against resource cost.

rules.statement: A gigantic bomb upgrades another bomb to affect a short area rather than an immediate area; an overpowered bomb adds 4 damage to a damage-inflicting bomb. Each upgrade is consumed when applied and then no longer counts toward the cypher limit.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Gigantic Bomb; Overpowered Bomb (cypher-rd#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one consumed upgrade per bomb; a world can alter upgrade availability, with the tradeoff being greater area or damage from a single-use resource.

rules.statement: A force field is level 6, conforms to available space without pressing on solid obstacles, blocks gas, and lasts until a one-hour recovery. A cube or sphere can contain foes after successful Intellect attacks against them.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Force field effect (cypher-rd#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the stated field shapes, duration, and containment check; a world can vary the field’s level or persistence, with stronger barriers being harder to obtain.

rules.statement: Some cyphers affect each creature in an area with separate attacks; on a failed attack, several still inflict reduced damage. Other effects specify a level threshold, such as being harder to affect when a target is level 7 or higher.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Cypher descriptions (cypher-rd#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to separate attacks and the stated success and failure outcomes; a world can adjust thresholds or failure damage, trading reliability against effect strength.

rules.statement: Resurrection works only on someone who died within the last hour, undoes the fatal injury or effect, and leaves the revived person hindered until recovery with one fewer permanent moderate-wound capacity. Revived NPCs instead suffer a 5-point maximum-health reduction, to a minimum of 1.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Resurrection (cypher-rd#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the one-hour window and permanent capacity cost; a world can change the window or cost, with resurrection’s lasting bodily consequences limiting repeated use.

rules.statement: Each level of Effort costs 3 points from the Pool suited to the task and eases it by one step; later levels cost 2 points each. Subtract the matching Edge once from the total Pool cost for an action, to a minimum of 0; attacks may instead use Effort to add 3 damage per level.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Easing Tasks — Effort; Edge (cypher-rd#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: apply Effort before rolling and discount its total cost once per action; a world can change the point costs or discount rule; the in-world cost is depletion of the relevant Pool.
