rules.statement: A task’s difficulty can be reduced by at most 11 steps in total: up to 3 from skill, 2 from assets, and 6 from Effort. An asset usually gives one step of ease, and assets together cannot give more than two.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Easing Tasks — Asset; Free Level of Effort (cypher-rd#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: enforce the stated source-specific caps and 11-step ceiling; a world can turn the caps up or down; the limit keeps stacked advantages from making tasks routine too easily.

rules.statement: A d20 result of 1 causes a GM-chosen complication without awarding XP. On a damage-dealing attack, 17 or 18 adds 1 or 2 damage; 19 adds 3 damage or grants a minor effect, and 20 adds 4 damage or grants a major effect, while also refunding all Pool points spent on that action.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Special Rolls; GM Intrusion; Damage Bonus (cypher-rd#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: apply these results only on the stated natural die faces; a world can change which results trigger them; the complication on a 1 and bonus effects on high rolls shape risk and reward.

rules.statement: After a failed task, another attempt is a new action taking the same time as the first and must use at least one level of Effort; further attempts each require Effort too. The GM may rule that no retry is possible, and a missed combat attack is not a retry because the situation changes each round.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Retrying a Task After Failure (cypher-rd#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: charge at least one Effort level for each retry; a world can make retries cheaper, costlier, or unavailable; repeated attempts consume the character’s Pool.

rules.statement: A character may move an immediate distance alongside an action, or use the whole action to move a short distance. Combining a short move with another task hinders all tasks until the end of the next turn; using the whole action to run a long distance hinders tasks by two steps for the same period.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Distance, Range, and Movement — Movement (cypher-rd#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: use the stated range categories and hindrances; a world can alter distances or penalties; moving quickly compromises the character’s other tasks.

rules.statement: Most ability durations that lack a more specific limit continue until the character takes a recovery of ten minutes or longer, which ends the effect. This lets the character preserve an ongoing effect by postponing recovery.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Timekeeping (cypher-rd#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: end such effects when a recovery of at least ten minutes is taken; a world can use fixed durations instead; delaying recovery preserves the effect but postpones restoring Pool points.

rules.statement: Each character gets one action per combat round, usually lasting about 5–10 seconds; a First action can resolve ahead of the normal initiative order, while a Last action resolves at round’s end and prevents other activity that round. A First action may be followed by a minor non-attack activity after everyone else acts.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Actions and Initiative — First Actions; Last Actions (cypher-rd#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: use one action per round and resolve First and Last actions at their specified points; a world can change action timing or availability; committing to a Last action gives up other activity that round.

rules.statement: An attack aimed at another creature or object requires a roll to hit or affect it unless the ability explicitly says otherwise. Ordinary attacks succeed when the roll meets or exceeds the target number; a missed touch-based ability is retained and can be retried on later turns until it hits or the user takes an incompatible action.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Attacks (cypher-rd#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to requiring a fresh roll for each attack; a setting can allow automatic hits for particular abilities, justified by exceptional precision or effect.

rules.statement: A core character can take three wounds at each of three severities. Once minor capacity is full, further minor wounds become moderate; once moderate capacity is full, further moderate wounds become major, and filling the third major wound kills the character. Each major wound hinders all actions, and a full moderate track also hinders all actions.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Wounds (cypher-rd#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to three boxes per severity with overflow and escalating penalties; a world can increase capacity or soften death, at the cost of making injury less consequential.

rules.statement: When damage reduces a character’s stat Pool to zero, later damage to that Pool—including excess from the same attack—becomes wounds: 1–4 points make a minor wound, 5–8 a moderate wound, and 9 or more a major wound.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Pool Damage to Wound Conversions (cypher-rd#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to converting depleted Pool damage into wounds at these thresholds; a world can change the thresholds to make depleted resources more or less dangerous.

rules.statement: NPC damage reduces health, commonly equal to three times the NPC’s level; at zero or less health the NPC is defeated. Physical Armor reduces incoming physical damage by its rating, while mental attacks generally ignore it; the attacker can choose whether a defeated NPC dies or is merely unconscious.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Inflicting Damage on NPCs (cypher-rd#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to health loss, physical Armor reduction, and attacker choice at defeat; a world can make defeat nonlethal or Armor apply more broadly, changing lethality and protection.

rules.statement: An object’s level serves as both Armor and health: a successful attack must exceed that protection before excess damage lowers its level point for point. At level zero it is broken; damage equal to its original level after that destroys it, and a physical tool too soft for the object cannot damage it.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Damage to Objects (cypher-rd#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to gradual level reduction followed by destruction; a world can use one-step breakage instead, trading durability detail for simplicity.

rules.statement: A character has four recoveries per day—one action, ten minutes, one hour, and ten hours. Each completed recovery restores a d6 plus tier points, freely divided among Pools up to their maxima; interruption delays its benefit until the full time is completed, and a one-action recovery used as a Last action adds 2 to its roll.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Recoveries (cypher-rd#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to four timed recoveries with tier-scaled restoration; a world can grant fewer or slower recoveries, making resource management more restrictive.

rules.statement: Wounds can be removed by spending Might for a quick rally—2 points for a minor or 5 for a moderate wound—or by treatment or rest; rallying normally cannot remove major wounds. A ten-minute recovery removes all minor wounds, an hour removes one moderate or all minor wounds, and ten hours removes all moderate wounds and may remove a major wound with a difficulty 6 Might task.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Healing Wounds (cypher-rd#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to these costs and recovery windows; a world can make treatment faster or allow rallying from major wounds, at the cost of reducing injury persistence.

rules.statement: Blocking uses a Might defense roll and on success reduces a wound by one severity; dodging uses Speed and on success avoids the wound entirely, though area attacks hinder dodging. A shield used in a successful block can take the whole wound instead, but it breaks when it takes a major wound; shields can absorb three minor, two moderate, and one major wound.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Defending; Armor and Shields (cypher-rd#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to choosing either block or dodge and to shield damage capacity as given; a world can make shields tougher or blocking less effective, changing the balance of defense and equipment loss.

rules.statement: After a failed defense, some continuing hostile effects can be challenged again by spending a recovery of the required duration; that attempt grants none of the recovery’s usual Pool restoration or wound removal. Disease instead calls for a Might defense each day, with failure applying its specified effect.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Other Defenses; Special Damage (cypher-rd#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to recovery-gated attempts to end ongoing effects and daily disease checks; a world can shorten or lengthen the interval, changing how long afflictions persist.

rules.statement: Spend 1 XP to reroll any roll, including another player’s; keep the better result, and repeat as many times as you can afford. XP may also be spent on recovery or artifact-depletion rolls.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Spending Experience Points — Rerolling (cypher-rd#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: allow repeat rerolls for 1 XP each; a world can restrict eligible rolls to make XP scarcer, reflecting that experience is a limited resource.

rules.statement: Spend 1 XP to introduce a beneficial change to the campaign. A player cannot refuse a GM intrusion, but may spend 1 XP on their next turn to soften its consequences without undoing it.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Player Intrusion; React to a GM Intrusion (cypher-rd#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: permit one beneficial player-authored change for 1 XP; a world can limit its scope, preserving the GM’s intrusion while giving the player a response.

rules.statement: A character begins at tier 1 and buys four different advancement options, each for 4 XP, before reaching the next tier; each option can be bought only once per tier. Advancements add 4 Pool points, +1 Edge, +1 Effort (maximum 6), or skill improvements, and each also grants resource points.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Character Advancement (cypher-rd#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: require four 4-XP purchases per tier; a world can vary the XP price or benefits to change advancement pace, reflecting how quickly experience turns into ability.

rules.statement: Spending 1 XP can make an attack against a foe whose location is unknown succeed as a lucky shot, but the attack is hindered by four steps. Without spending the XP, the attack automatically fails.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Lucky Shot (cypher-rd#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: allow the costly, four-step-hindered shot; a world can forbid it, making uncertainty and impaired senses absolute barriers.

rules.statement: Each character advancement grants 1 resource point, rising to 2 per advancement at tier 3 and 3 at tier 5; the GM may award more. Resource points represent time, access, luck, and other means of achieving a chosen goal.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Resource Points — Gaining Resource Points (cypher-rd#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: award 1, 2, or 3 points according to tier; a world can award extra points when circumstances help, representing unusually available resources or opportunity.

rules.statement: After the required time has passed, spending resource points usually completes a goal without a roll. Crafting a genre-appropriate cypher costs 2 points for low power with trained crafting, 3 for medium power with specialized crafting, or 4 for advanced power with expert crafting.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Goals and Activities; Cypher Crafting Requirements (cypher-rd#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: require the listed training, point cost, and time; a world can alter costs or crafting access to reflect how difficult its technology or magic is to make.

rules.statement: With trained crafting, spend 1 resource point to craft or repair a genre-appropriate object up to level 4; higher-level or higher-technology work costs more and requires at least specialized crafting. A specialized or expert crafter can spend 5 or more points to make a genre-appropriate artifact up to level 5, usually with one benefit.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Craft Object; Repair Object; Craft Artifact (cypher-rd#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: cap ordinary work at level 4 and artifacts at level 5; a world can raise costs or restrict materials to reflect its crafting capabilities.

rules.statement: Resource points can restore a lost follower to their healthy, active state for half the follower’s level in points, rounded up to at least 1; this usually takes several days or about a week if no duration is specified. Research costs 1 point for information level 1–3, 2 for level 4–5, and 3 for level 6–7; higher-level information normally requires play rather than points.
locators: Cypher Reference Document: Restore Follower; Research (cypher-rd#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: allow restoration and research only within their stated costs and time or level limits; a world can raise those limits, making recovery or secrets harder to obtain through downtime.
